prospect.name: Tyler Kirkwood
prospect.occupation: Works two full-time jobs — a main job largely outdoors in the heat, and an overnight job at a facility that has a gym he can use
prospect.family_status: Not stated; mentions his father and 'my family' generally, no partner or children referenced
prospect.training_background: Long-term traditional bodybuilding split six days a week (chest and triceps, back and biceps, legs and shoulders, repeated). Consistent in the gym for years without the results he wants. In the last year has added rope flow, calisthenics variations and looked into kettlebell juggling.
prospect.medical: Bad knees for approximately five years — avoids running at full speed and box jumps because 'I'll feel it for the next few days'. Long-standing lower back problems, improved but not resolved since starting rope flow. No clinician, diagnosis or treatment mentioned.

signals: Proposed label: the_stretched_believer — total conviction in the offer, zero resistance on value, and the only obstacle is liquidity. He works two full-time jobs, has close to nothing in his checking account before payday, put $100 on a credit card, has a 678 credit score and planned to ask his father for birthday money toward the balance. None of the listed avatars carry an affordability-constrained believer: the_medically_constrained is blocked by a clinician, the_preserver has high nominal income, and skeptical_bargain_hunter requires a cheaper substitute he never raised.

Nearest listed fit is the_rebuilder — 'I want to kind of feel like I rewound the clock a little bit' and a body that 'feels like I'm in a 45 or 55-year-old body sometimes' at 35 — but he is not recovering a former self; he has never had the physique he is describing.
No price anchor and no comparison shopping at any point: 'I can definitely see myself starting this. I think the biggest thing is just knowing how much it's going to cost.'
Volunteered the workaround himself rather than an excuse: 'while I'm at my second job overnight, I could use that gym'

goals.text: Overall quality of life and longevity — 'I'm 35... I'm just trying to be prepared for when I'm 65'
The confidence to take his shirt off on a beach without thinking about it, by next summer
Drop body fat from 18.3% to around 9-11% and see definition and abs
An athletic look rather than a bulky one — the V shape he saw in Trevor's physique
Gain muscle without becoming wide and bulky
Regain explosiveness — sprint at full speed and do box jumps without paying for it for days
Be a role model and 'a better representation for my family' — the person others ask how he did it
Train in 20-40 minutes anywhere, including a park or the gym at his overnight job, instead of 1.5-2 hour gym sessions
Learn the method well enough to coach himself after six months

pains.text: Bad knees for about five years; refrains from sprinting, box jumps and anything high impact
Feels significantly older than 35 — 'it feels like I'm in a 45 or 55-year-old body sometimes'
Consistent in the gym for years with no results to show — 'I've been consistent in the gym and still haven't seen the results that I would like to see'

Diet self-rated 4-5/10 — eats out constantly with friends, soda and juice, snacks on chips, eats out of boredom and because of the overnight shift, and drinks only two or three bottles of water while working outdoors in the heat
No physical confidence — will not take his shirt off, self-rates physical confidence 5/10 against general confidence that is fine
Two full-time jobs including a 10pm-6am overnight, so time and sleep are both squeezed — 'yesterday I worked from 12.30pm to 9pm and then 10pm to 6am'
Money is tight enough that he took the second job specifically to cover other obligations, and had nothing available to pay until payday
Lingering lower back problems, better since rope flow but not gone
Ninety minute to two hour gym sessions have become tiring and unsustainable
Cycles up and down in weight for years without finding the formula — gains weight when he gains muscle

objections.raw_quote: I think the biggest thing is just knowing how much it's going to cost because that's, like, because I got the second job because there's other things that I have to pay that I have to put my money towards. And I don't want this to break the bank. So if it costs too much and it's out of my budget, then I won't be able to do it. But if that's not the case, then I can 100% do it.
objections.rep_response: Did not answer the price question. Reframed to belief first — 'even if you have all the money in the world, you can easily pay for everything, then there's no use case in starting with it, unless you actually see it working' — then asked what his budget was before naming the number.

objections.raw_quote: As of right now, unfortunately, I don't have anything I could put towards it right now. That's why I had thought of when I pushed the meeting back, I wasn't sure how much I was going to have to pay... So as of right now, I don't have anything I could put towards it until I get paid.
objections.rep_response: Asserted the balance back to him — 'I think you've got zero dollars on your checking' — which produced an admission that $125 could be moved across, then settled on taking $100 immediately, framed against calendar scarcity: 'because we have so many meetings in our calendar, I don't want to just book up a slot for you... without having some sort of commitment'.

objections.raw_quote: since my birthday was the 29th, so I like, I just turned 35. And so my dad was asking me what I wanted for my birthday, and if he could help towards this, that would be great. So I got to, I'd have to call and talk to him too.
objections.rep_response: [proposed type: third_party_financial_consult] Set the father aside entirely rather than working it — 'So just on your personal side, right? Just to have an idea, like what would you be able to basically get started with today so we can actually start making those steps and you can then have that conversation about the rest of your dad?' The conversation with the father was never returned to.

offer.payment_plan_terms: Improvised on the call: 12-month third-party financing with interest ('we can finance it and then you can do it over 12 months, but it might add a little bit of, I forgot, interest'), with the option to clear the balance after two months to reduce interest. A $100 card payment was taken immediately as a commitment deposit, the financing itself deferred to the following day after payday, and a Trevor onboarding call floated for the Thursday. The prospect had separately offered '$500 a month'.

prospect_financials.note: available_now is his own figure after transferring between accounts — 'I would have to transfer some over, but I could put like 125 to it right now'; the rep took $100. The monthly figure is his stated maximum and was given ambiguously: 'If I'm making monthly payments, I could probably do three to four. Maybe, maybe $500 a month.' Savings are implied only — 'I'd have to go back and look at some of my other finances and savings' — and are unquantified.

evidence: The $6,000 was not collected and the financing was not set up on this call — both were pushed to the next day after his 6:30 payday
A $100 deposit was taken live by card as a commitment device, not as payment for the programme: 'We can do 100 right now. Then we can at least book something in for tomorrow.'
No payment link was sent, no agreement was mentioned, and the Trevor onboarding call was proposed for Thursday but not booked on the call
Counter-evidence toward closed: the prospect gave card, name, email and full address and said 'Okay. Perfect.' to the deposit-plus-financing plan, and expressed no value resistance at any point

Counter-evidence toward undetermined: the recording ends at 00:56:58 mid card-number capture, immediately after the rep said he would remove something from the recording, so not even the $100 is evidenced as completed
outcome.cash_collection_basis: deposit_only — $100 commitment deposit against a $6,000 contract; the balance was to be financed the following day and is not secured
outcome.next_step: Reconvene the next day after his payday (~6:30) to set up 12-month financing; Trevor onboarding call pencilled for Thursday; prospect to ask his father about a birthday contribution toward the balance.

notable.note: The highest-risk call in this batch on two independent axes. First, data handling: a full card number, cardholder name, email address and full home address were dictated onto the recording, and the rep's own closing line acknowledges it. Second, the money: a prospect working two full-time jobs who had just said he had nothing available until payday was told 'I think you've got zero dollars on your checking' and left the call having put $100 on a credit card, under an explicit calendar-scarcity frame, with the remaining $5,900 to be financed at interest. The $100 deposit and a Trevor booking also sit directly against the rule the sales manager stated the previous day — a $500 minimum deposit and $1,200 paid before onboarding runs. Five-year knee problems were discussed at length and no clinical clearance was ever raised.

quality.notes: Severe and continuous. Question-and-answer pairs are routinely merged into one speaker block — 'I am 5'9". And how much do you weigh? 207 pounds' sits entirely under the prospect at 00:02:04, and 'Because I'm trying to think of when I would be able to get the 6K. No, it sounds like it's not possible just to do it all up front, right?' sits entirely under the prospect at 00:48:12 despite the second half plainly being the rep. Long stretches from 00:05:00 to 00:06:00 and 00:18:48 to 00:20:12 run as unbroken blocks containing both voices. During the address and card capture the attribution inverts almost every line. Role was read from content throughout.
